Research Article

Advances in modifications of Ag/g-C3N4 for stable and effective
photoanode for OER
Hira Jabeen c, Rida Shahzadi Haider d, e, Shamaila Sajjad a, c, *, Sajjad Ahmed Khan Leghari b,
Saima Noor c, Mohammed A. Amin f, Mohamed M. Ibrahim f

A R T I C L E I N F O A B S T R A C T

Keywords: Silver (Ag) incorporated graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) nano-composites having various ratios of Ag were
Ag/g-C3N4 prepared via a chemical route. The synthesized catalysts were potentially employed in an oxygen evolution
Photoelectrochemical process reaction (OER) through photoelectrochemical (PEC). An XRD profile of Ag/g-C3N4 nano-composite depicted
Oxygen evolution reaction
 hexagonal g-C3N4 along with FCC Ag presence. The inhomogeneous distribution of tiny Ag nanospheres on
Open-circuit voltage
 irregularly agglomerated sheets of g-C3N4 was clearly seen in SEM images. The elemental mapping provided
Water splittiing
 distribution of elements in the composite sample. Ag/g-C3N4 nano-composite samples show improvement in
 absorption edge with a reduction in band gap energy. FTIR studies illustrated strong surface interaction among
 Ag and g-C3N4 nano-sheets. The prominent reduction in PL peaks intensity for B30 Ag/g-C3N4 nano-composite
 suggested a long lifetime of photo induced charge carriers. XPS analysis confirmed the existence of metallic
 Ag on g-C3N4. B30 Ag/g-C3N4 attained better PEC activity results as compared to all other prepared photo­
 catalysts. In OER experiments, B30 Ag/g-C3N4 showed a small onset potential (0.33 V) leading to more pro­
 duction of photo excited electrons and a reduction in photo generated electron-hole recombination process. The
 improved Jsc and Voc of B30 Ag/g-C3N4 indicated the shorter lifetime of charge carriers across electrode and
 electrolyte interface through suitable charge separation. Optimized B30 Ag/g-C3N4 is active and steady for
 efficient PEC water splitting in comparison to other prepared nanosystems.

of a few nanometers [29,30]. Nano-sheets of g-C3N4 offer more active
sites for photocatalytic reactions. It is clearly seen in the SEM image of
B30 Ag/g-C3N4 nano-composite that the stacked sheets of g-C3N4 are
fully covered by dots like structures of Ag nanoparticles. The homoge­
nous distribution of Ag shows a strong attachment on g-C3N4 sheets with
highly active sites which are favourable in capturing of visible light
photons during PEC activity. EDX analysis of g-C3N4 and B30 Ag/g-C3N4
indicated the constituent elements (N, O, C) and (C, N, O and Ag) of both
samples, respectively. This confirms the purity of pure and composite
materials. Furthermore, the distribution of elements of B30 Ag/g-C3N4
composite has been confirmed by elemental mapping images. Red,
purple, yellow and green colours showed the existence of C, N, Ag and O,
respectively. Both EDX and elemental mapping results contain oxygen
contents due to samples preparation in the air atmosphere [31].

 3.8. PEC activity

 PEC measurements of photocatalysts were conducted by LSV in 0.07
 M KOH electrolyte at pH ∼ 12.8 and λ > 420 nm at a scan rate of 10
 mvsec− 1 (Fig. 7B). Applied potential is converted into reversible
 hydrogen electrode (RHE). Under visible light exposure, pure g-C3N4
 photoanode shows lower current density in contrast to Ag NPs decorated
 g-C3N4 photocatalyst. Incorporated Ag NPs on g-C3N4 affected the
 overall water splitting because of their surface plasmon resonance.
 When it is excited by visible light, it shows better absorption. However,
 Ag NPs decorated g-C3N4 with the incorporation of increasing contents
